methodology_note: IMPORTANT: On this machine with Ultralytics/PyTorch, when a CUDA-capable GPU is visible (torch.cuda.is_available()=True), model.predict(device='cpu') does not produce clean CPU-only inference. The GPU is used for some graph operations and predict() blocks on GPU sync, producing ~12000ms/tick instead of ~27ms. Clean CPU inference (27ms) is only achievable with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' (GPU fully masked). Since production always has GPU visible, the meaningful comparison is GPU (cuda:0) vs CPU with GPU masked.

cpu_isolated.label: CPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' -- GPU fully masked)
cpu_isolated.note: This is the clean CPU performance when no GPU is visible. Not representative of production (GPU is always present).

cpu_gpu_visible.label: CPU (device='cpu', GPU visible, torch.cuda.is_available()=True)
cpu_gpu_visible.note: Pathological: Ultralytics/PyTorch performs implicit GPU sync even on cpu device when GPU is visible. NOT usable as a production CPU baseline.

stage24_cpu_reference.label: CPU reference (Stage 24 -- separate process, GPU visible but Ultralytics may have used CUDA implicitly)
stage24_cpu_reference.note: Stage 24 ran with YOLO_DEVICE='0' which resolved ambiguously. Results may reflect GPU usage via Ultralytics auto-detection.

reason: On this machine (Ultralytics + CUDA-visible GPU), device='cpu' does not produce clean CPU-only inference -- GPU sync overhead makes it unusable (~12000ms/tick). The only valid fast inference path is cuda:0 (~26.5ms YOLO, ~38.8ms total tick, 25.8 FPS). cuda:0 is confirmed as the correct and only practical production default on this hardware.
